questions.prompt: What is implied here about the pound at Owlerby?

options.text: The pound was probably a useful source of income for the parish in these years.
An owner's bill turned on which day of the week his beast was taken up.
Because the table charged by the night, a heavy bill marked an owner slow to miss his beast.
Skellorne decided how long a beast stayed in the pound, and a longer stay paid him better.
